Prostate-specific antigen monitoring
Measurement of PSA is the cornerstone of follow-up after local treatment. While PSA thresholds depend on the
local treatment used, PSA recurrence almost always precedes clinical recurrence [1436, 1437]. The key question
is to establish when a PSA rise is clinically significant since not all PSA increases have the same clinical value
(see Section 6.4.2) [994]. No prospective studies are available on the optimal timing for PSA testing and the
impact on oncological outcomes.

interventions.body:
WHAT I FOUND
**radiology_report**: The mpMRI Prostate exam showed a focal lesion in the peripheral zone, mid to apex left, measuring approximately 18 mm. This lesion demonstrated restricted diffusion on DWI with corresponding early enhancement on DCE, consistent with PI-RADS 5. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion was visualized. Impression: PI-RADS 5 lesion, peripheral zone mid/apex left. Clinical stage: cT1c.
**pathology_report**: The biopsy revealed adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 4+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 4. The growth pattern was predominantly cribriform, with a cribriform pattern identified as a high-risk feature. The tumour was located in the peripheral zone, mid/apex left. Summary: The biopsy trajectory showed a stable high-grade disease profile across the evaluated timepoint. AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 5.
**previous_notes**: A note from Dr. C. Peters (GP) dated 27 Feb 2024 indicates the patient presented with PSA 1.1 ng/mL, significantly lower than the previous value of 15.7 ng/mL. The decision was made to continue routine monitoring without immediate intervention, with follow-up scheduled for early 2025 to reassess PSA dynamics.
**family_history**: No family history of prostate cancer was recorded.
**psa_trend**: The PSA trend shows values of 1.7 ng/mL in Apr 2022, 15.7 ng/mL in Mar 2023, 1.1 ng/mL in Mar 2024, and 70.0 ng/mL in Feb 2025.
**laboratory_results**: Laboratory results include a PSA of 70.0 ng/mL (dated 27 Jan 2025), Free PSA of 15.70 ng/mL, %Free PSA of 22%, Haemoglobin of 15.3 g/dL, WBC of 6.9 x10^9/L, Platelets of 230 x10^9/L, Creatinine of 69 umol/L, eGFR >60 mL/min/1.73m2, Testosterone of 14.7 nmol/L, Alkaline phosphatase of 80 U/L, LDH of 135 U/L, and HbA1c of 6.3 %.

WHAT IS NOT RECORDED
The specific findings from the MRI scan that informed the PI-RADS 5 assessment were not explicitly detailed in the initial intake, although the report itself is retrieved. The family history was not recorded.
